name: gtx1080
description: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 (GP104, Pascal, sm_61) at its 1607 MHz base clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 20 SMs, 64 resident warps/SM, 4 schedulers x 32 lanes (NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 whitepaper)
sources.DCACHE_SIZE: 48 KB unified L1/texture per SM (whitepaper): 6 ways over power-of-two sets
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 2 MB L2 (whitepaper); 16 ways, 16 banks for the 16 memory channels
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 256-bit GDDR5X at 10 Gbps modelled as 16 GDDR6 x16 channels at 10000 MT/s: 16 x 2 B x 10 GT/s = 320 GB/s, the card's bandwidth; latency not calibrated
sources.FETCH_WIDTH: 4 SM processing blocks, each with its own instruction buffer and warp scheduler (NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 (GP104) whitepaper)
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock per SM: 32 banks of 4 B on the part (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, shared memory). Vortex banks are XLEN wide (8 B), so 16 banks carry the same bytes per clock; lanes reading one 8 B word share its bank access, so a stride-1 FP32 warp read is conflict-free as on the part
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Every NVIDIA GPU since Pascal has a demand-paged MMU (unified memory), global and shared-memory atomics with a native compare-and-swap (atomicCAS), FP16 storage and conversion, and per-partition special-function units for the transcendentals (TFU)
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE: Pascal has no tensor cores and no RT cores
sources.xlen: 64-bit machine: 64-bit pointers and FP64 (the D extension follows XLEN=64), with a 48-bit device address space against NVIDIA's 49-bit virtual addresses; configure --profile picks a build64 tree and a build32 tree rejects the profile
sources.NUM_BARRIERS: 16 named CTA barriers (bar.sync 0-15, PTX ISA) on every NVIDIA GPU
sources.EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_OM_ENABLE: Raster engines in every GPC and ROPs in every memory partition (architecture whitepaper)
sources.NUM_TFU_LANES: 32 special-function results per clock per SM (8 SFUs in each of the 4 processing blocks) for the reciprocal, reciprocal square root, log2, exp2, sine and cosine (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 6.1)
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: GP104 SM (GTX 1080 whitepaper): 4 processing blocks, each with 32 CUDA cores (FP32 and INT32 on the same cores), 8 LD/ST units and 8 SFUs; 4 FP64 cores per SM. One Vortex ALU/FPU/LSU block per processing block (ISSUE_WIDTH=4) with the part's INT32, FP32 and LD/ST lanes; a 32-thread warp instruction issues over NUM_THREADS/lanes cycles, as on the part. The TCU stays full-warp (NUM_TCU_LANES == NUM_THREADS). FP64 FMAs run on their own F64 FMA PE (FMA64_PE_RATIO)
sources.FMA64_PE_RATIO: FP64 FMA at 1/32 of the FP32 rate: 4 FP64 cores per SM, 1 per processing block (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 6.1); 32 FPU lanes / 32 = 1 F64 FMA PE. FP64 division, square root and conversions take the FDIV/FSQRT/FCVT rates
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO: 32 results per clock per SM, 8 per processing block: FP32 reciprocal and reciprocal square root, on which division and square root are built (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 6.1); 32 FPU lanes / 4
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE, DCACHE_SIZE: 96 KB dedicated shared memory per SM, separate from the 48 KB L1/texture (GTX 1080 whitepaper), in a 128 KB window
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies: Jia et al., Dissecting the NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking (arXiv 1903.07486), Table 3.1: L1 hit 82 and L2 hit ~216 cycles on the Tesla P4, a GP104 like this card. No DRAM latency is published for GP104, so dram_cycles is unchecked. Accel-Sim correlates the Pascal TITAN X and GTX 1080 Ti (posted hardware runs: pascal-titanx, pascal-1080ti)
sources.L1_LINK_LATENCY: 26 core cycles each way between a core and its dcache, the L1/texture load pipeline, which the dcache bank pipeline (DCACHE_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the 82-cycle L1 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 52 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py (after the L1 link) so the SimX pointer chase gives the 216-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: Not set: no DRAM latency is published for this part, so dram_cycles is unchecked
